did_you_know.text: Cities of refuge protected someone who had killed accidentally until he could receive a fair trial. They were not meant to shelter a deliberate murderer.
The command to prepare the roads to the cities of refuge shows that justice also depends on accessibility. According to the Sages, signs reading “Refuge” were placed along the roads.
The “avenger of blood” was a relative who sought to avenge a family member’s death. The law tries to stop him from killing someone who caused an accidental death in the heat of emotion.
In ancient times, field boundaries were sometimes marked with stones. Moving a boundary stone was a way to take part of a neighbor’s land by deception.
Requiring more than one witness is a legal principle meant to prevent conviction based on a single accusation. It calls for supporting evidence before declaring someone guilty.
The verse commands judges to examine testimony carefully rather than accept it automatically. This places responsibility not only on witnesses, but also on the justice system.

The phrase “an eye for an eye” sounds like physical retaliation, but the Sages interpreted it as financial compensation for the injury. In this way, the principle became a measure of damages rather than an encouragement of revenge.
